CHIEF COMPLAINT
Acne on the face

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 18-year-old female presenting with acne located on the face that started approximately two years ago and is present most every day. She denies associated symptoms including itching, bleeding, or pain. She reports that acne is not too bad on the chest or back. She has been using Persa-Gel and washing regularly, which she reports is somewhat helpful. She notes that today is a good day for her acne. Acne does not flare with menses. Mother reports that the biggest flare occurred when patient started school sports in the fall due to sweating. Patient reports good compliance with facial care regimen but notes that it has not helped as much as desired.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies itching, bleeding, or pain associated with acne. Gets regular menses, started approximately two years ago.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No additional past medical history.

MEDICATIONS
Elf Super Clarity Cleanser (nighttime)
Toner (nighttime)
Persa-Gel (nighttime)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
No additional family history.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives with parents and sister. Has a dog, bird, and bunnies. In 7th grade. Plays basketball, volleyball, and tap. Wears sunscreen SPF 30 in the summer.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Full exam performed except under underwear and under bra. Multiple benign nevi on trunk and extremities. Scattered skin-colored papules, open and closed comedones, and erythematous papules on face, primarily on forehead with some on central cheeks and chin. Chest and back relatively spared. Remainder of examination normal.

RESULTS
Mild to moderate acne, mostly comedonal with small inflammatory component. Multiple benign moles on arms, legs, back, and abdomen with no worrisome features.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Mild to moderate acne. Starting topical therapy: Morning regimen includes mild cleanser followed by noncomedogenic moisturizer with SPF 30 or higher. Evening regimen includes mild cleanser, then adapalene 0.1% cream applied in thin layer to areas of acne, starting a few nights per week and slowly working up to every night (alternative over-the-counter gel if cost or insurance coverage is an issue), followed by Clean and Clear Persa-Gel in thin layer, then noncomedogenic moisturizer. Patient counseled on need for sunscreen use while outside due to sensitivity from retinoid. Discussed potential side effects including dryness and irritation. Will monitor benign moles and follow up in six months to assess progress.
